title: Serve a valid robots.txt at the root of every public host
statement: Each public host answers a request for its root robots.txt path with a 200 and a plain-text body that parses under the Robots Exclusion Protocol, with no HTML error page and no redirect to another host.
rationale: A body that fails to parse or arrives as an HTML page leaves the crawler with no usable directives, so the rules the site believes are in force are simply absent for that host.
implementation: Serve the file from the host root rather than a subdirectory, with a text media type. If the framework generates it, confirm the generated output for each configured host, because a single shared file cannot express host-specific rules.

verification.method: Request the root robots.txt path on each public host and parse the returned body against the protocol grammar, recording status and media type.

title: Reference the sitemap index from the robots.txt of the host it covers
statement: The robots.txt file names its sitemap or sitemap index with an absolute URL, and that URL is on the same host that served the robots.txt.
rationale: The Sitemap directive is how a crawler finds the submission without being told, and a directive pointing at a different host describes a file the crawler will not treat as authoritative for this one.
implementation: Emit the directive from the same configuration that decides the production origin, so the two cannot drift. When several sitemaps exist, name the index rather than listing each child file.

verification.method: Read the Sitemap directives out of the served robots.txt, then request each named URL and record its host and status.

sources.title: Sitemaps XML format, sitemap location in robots.txt

title: Keep robots.txt groups free of rules that contradict each other
statement: For any given crawler, the rule that the protocol's longest-match precedence selects is the rule the site intends, and no wildcard group silently overrides a more specific group in a way the author did not plan.
rationale: Precedence is decided by match length rather than by file order, so a group that looks like a narrowing exception can turn out to be inert while a broad rule elsewhere is the one actually applied.
implementation: For each path the site cares about, evaluate the whole file the way the protocol does and record which rule wins. Keep one group per agent rather than several, and express exceptions as longer allow patterns beneath the disallow they modify.

verification.method: Run a protocol-conformant matcher over a list of representative paths for each declared user-agent group and record the winning rule for each pair.

title: Apply a noindex directive only where exclusion from the index is intended
statement: Every page carrying a robots noindex directive is on a list of pages the site has decided should not be indexed, and no page outside that list carries one.
rationale: A noindex directive removes a page from search entirely, and because nothing about the rendered page looks different, one left behind by a template default or a staging build can stay unnoticed indefinitely.
implementation: Write the intended exclusion list down as data and derive the directive from it, rather than setting it per template. Never add or remove the directive on a page without first confirming which side of that list the page belongs on.

verification.method: Collect the robots directives from both the meta element and the response header of every sampled route and compare the resulting set against the intended exclusion list.

sources.title: Robots meta tag, data-nosnippet, and X-Robots-Tag specifications

title: Control indexing of non-HTML responses with an X-Robots-Tag header
statement: Where a PDF, image, feed, or other non-HTML response needs an indexing directive, that directive is carried in the X-Robots-Tag response header, since the format cannot hold a meta element.
rationale: These resources are indexed on their own, and without a header there is no mechanism to express any directive for them at all, so the site's intent for the file has no representation in the response.
implementation: Set the header where the response is produced - the file-serving route, the storage bucket metadata, or an edge rule keyed on path or media type. Confirm the CDN forwards it, and prefer a rule keyed on the resource path over one keyed on extension alone.

verification.method: Request each non-HTML resource that needs a directive and read the X-Robots-Tag value from the response headers.

sources.title: Robots meta tag, data-nosnippet, and X-Robots-Tag specifications

title: Mark sponsored and user-generated links with the documented rel values
statement: Outbound links that were paid for carry rel=sponsored, links inside user-submitted content carry rel=ugc, and neither category is left with a bare href or with rel=nofollow used as a catch-all.
rationale: These values are the documented way to tell an engine how a link came to exist, and paid links left unmarked fall under published link-spam policy rather than being merely untagged.
implementation: Apply the value where the link's provenance is known: the advertising component adds sponsored, the user-content renderer adds ugc to every external href it emits. Do not add these values to the site's own internal navigation.

verification.method: Extract outbound anchors from pages that render paid placements or user submissions and record the rel token list on each.

sources.title: Qualify your outbound links to Google
Spam policies for Google web search, link spam

title: Resolve disagreement between crawl directives and index directives
statement: No path is disallowed in robots.txt while also relying on a meta or header directive to control its indexing, because a crawler that cannot fetch the page cannot read the directive inside it.
rationale: Blocking the fetch hides the noindex rather than enforcing it, so the URL can still appear in results from external signals alone, which is the opposite of the intended outcome.
implementation: Decide which of the two mechanisms expresses the intent for each path. To keep a page out of the index, allow the fetch and serve the noindex; to keep a crawler off a path entirely, disallow it and accept that its indexing cannot then be controlled from the response.

verification.method: Cross-reference the disallowed path patterns against the routes that emit an index-suppressing directive and list every path matched by both.
